Draft A narrows to a single dimension (date calculation accuracy) and frames it as an open question without grounding in the user's actual reported results. It cites only F1–F2 (model composition and test setup) but omits the concrete performance differences (F3–F7) that motivated the original post. This creates a generic inquiry disconnected from the source's specific findings.

Draft B preserves all seven facts: the merge composition, test environment, and the three task outcomes (file-packing success, correct date calculation vs. incorrect competitor result, riddle solution vs. infinite loop). It acknowledges the single-user, early-2025 limitation and frames actionable questions about whether merging improves reasoning consistency and how to evaluate merges beyond anecdotal data. This grounds community discussion in the user's actual observations rather than speculation.

A's narrowing to date calculation alone loses the file-packing and infinite-loop findings—key evidence of the merge's impact. B's inclusion of all three tasks and explicit performance contrasts (19,121 vs. 19,486 days; single crossing vs. loop termination) gives readers concrete material to discuss and compare against their own tests. B also directly addresses the brief's desired response: exploring the user's observations and implications of model merging. A's open-ended framing risks becoming a generic reasoning-task question unmoored from the source.
